highlights.name: The online store
highlights.text: A bilingual Arabic and English storefront on Salla, fed by a product pipeline that delivers 12,700 SKUs with images, brands and three-level categories straight from the ERP.

highlights.name: Store and ERP in sync
highlights.text: Products, stock, orders, customers and brands flow both ways in real time through webhooks, with scheduled jobs as a fallback. Parallel workers and batching turned a multi-day sync into about an hour.

highlights.name: The 20-minute POS freeze
highlights.text: Cashiers waited up to half an hour for the POS to open, and loyalty rewards crashed the screen. We traced it to a third-party loading module and preloaded the reward products, without touching the vendor's code. The POS now opens in seconds.

highlights.name: An audit trail on everything
highlights.text: Who changed what, on every record, with user, device and session captured, and no slowdown at checkout.

highlights.name: Shop-floor stock counts
highlights.text: Staff count stock with handheld barcode scanners; confirmed counts adjust inventory automatically, with a full before-and-after history.

highlights.name: Competitor price monitor
highlights.text: Paste any competitor's product link and the system checks the price on a schedule, keeps the history and sends alerts when prices move.

highlights.name: Reports and sales targets
highlights.text: One-click profit, loss and vendor reports that can email themselves daily, weekly or monthly, plus live sales-target cards for every employee.

highlights.name: Also built
highlights.text: A customer self-order kiosk, receipt printing from the browser, price labels in eight formats with full Arabic support, expiry tracking and a product API.

osg.summary: An independent studio making mobile and PC games, including co-developments with major publishers. We fixed player-reported bugs across their mobile titles.
osg.intro: Mobile players don't file bug reports. They leave one-star reviews. The job was to find the bug behind each complaint, reproduce it on real devices, and ship a fix small enough to trust in a live game.
approach: Reproduce first: every fix starts from a player's report and a reliable way to trigger it.
Test on low-end Android phones, where most players actually are.
Ship the smallest fix that solves the problem, so nothing else breaks.
Protect player progress above everything else.

fixes.name: Negative gold after a few days away
fixes.problem: An idle game calculated offline earnings in a number type that overflowed after about a day. Returning players came back to negative gold.
fixes.fix: Moved the maths to a wider type, capped the offline window at the design limit, and made sure currency can never drop below its previous value.

fixes.name: Lost progress when Android closed the app
fixes.problem: If the phone killed the app in the middle of saving, the save file was left half-written and players lost everything.
fixes.fix: Saves now go to a temporary file first and replace the real one in a single step. The last good save is kept as a backup and checked before loading.

fixes.name: Stutter on budget phones
fixes.problem: Every coin pickup created and destroyed a particle effect. On low-end phones, the memory clean-up showed up as visible stutter in the busiest screens.
fixes.fix: Pooled the effects: a handful are prepared in advance and reused, so collecting coins costs almost nothing.

osg.code_title: What the save fix looks like
osg.code_note: Examples are simplified and stripped of the studio's code, but each is a real kind of bug we fixed.
osg.vault_text: A small arcade game we built in plain JavaScript: smooth 60 fps on phones and desktops, touch and keyboard controls, and difficulty that ramps as you play.
